newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan governor says won't withdraw resignation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan governor says won't withdraw resignation.

text.p: Taiwan governor James Soong, who resigned three weeks ago to protest a plan to dismantle his administration, said on Tuesday he was determined to go, but would return to work before his resignation is approved.
"My strong determination to resign has not changed a bit," Soong, the first elected provincial governor, said at a provincial government meeting.
Soong nonetheless said he would return to work before the central government agreed to his resignation.
"I will take the responsibility....patiently wait for the approval of my resignation," Soong said.
The 54-year-old Soong resigned on December 31, three days after the ruling Nationalist Party and main opposition Democratic Progressive Party agreed that all provincial elections should be frozen.

The agreement gave a strong boost to a central government drive to radically pare or even eliminate the Taichung-based provincial government in the name of eliminating redundancy in the many areas where the two huge administrations overlap.
